name: A Certain Ratio
label: Factory Records
lede: A Certain Ratio gave Factory its first single by a lone band, played funk in army-surplus shorts, cut a cover for £50 and once had Madonna as the opening act. Kerr, Moscrop and Johnson are still at it.

eras.title: Short back and sides in Hulme
eras.text: Four friends from Flixton and the Manchester Youth Theatre crowd, living on the dole in Hulme, with no drummer for a year and a look borrowed from the Oxfam rack. Within months of meeting Joy Division's manager they had Tony Wilson as manager, Martin Hannett as producer and a Factory single.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Write Wyatt · The Quietus
years.h: A Certain Ratio takes its name from a Brian Eno song
years.p: [[Simon Topping|6dd95305-7ca6-464d-a9de-93c3a963cda9]], [[Peter Terrell|d6a1837d-aacb-49be-8c64-0bbbea680489]], Jez Kerr and [[Martin Moscrop|0966e7ae-08f3-4923-adda-1a220212264d]] start a band in Flixton, Greater Manchester, named after a phrase in Eno's The True Wheel. For about a year they play without a drummer.
years.xp:
Kerr came to the band sideways. A broken ankle had ended his time in Manchester United's youth team at 17, and he met Topping and Terrell through the Manchester Youth Theatre. "I didn't know anything about it," he told Write Wyatt. "It was only through Gordon the Moron and the Youth Theatre that I met up with these people."

The look came from the same streets: demob suits, white shirts and army-surplus shorts from Oxfam, the Salvation Army and the army and navy store next door. "Everyone else was like spiky hair, we looked like bank managers," Kerr told the Quietus.

years.cap: A Certain Ratio at the Rock Garden, Covent Garden
years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton · Write Wyatt · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · The Quietus
years.h: Rob Gretton spots them on a bill with Joy Division
years.p: At a Manchester Musicians Collective night at Band on the Wall, Joy Division's manager [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]] sees ACR and sends them to Tony Wilson. Wilson takes them on and calls them "the new Sex Pistols."
years.xp:
Kerr remembers the band having "about six tunes" at the time. Wilson offered to manage them after seeing them play the Factory club night at the Russell Club in Hulme, where Moscrop and the others had been watching Suicide, Cabaret Voltaire, [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] and PiL.

Ban Ban Ton Ton's interview notes that [[Ian Curtis|10ae1bf6-88b2-4fb4-8fbe-8227a49803d3]] reportedly named ACR his favorite Factory band. Kerr later played down Wilson's role: "He was the manager in the early days, but he soon stopped that 'cos he was not really a manager."

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Write Wyatt
years.h: All Night Party is FAC 5, Factory's first single by one band
years.p: Martin Hannett produces. The 5,000 copies sell out.

years.src: Attack Magazine · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Wilson finds "the funkiest drummer in Manchester"
years.p: Wilson brings in [[Donald Johnson|49569ee1-aba3-4c08-8ead-9791a7f8c96d]], and the drummerless band becomes a rhythm section. Johnson is on the John Peel session cut on October 1 and broadcast on the 17th.
years.xp: The Peel session ran "Do the Du," "All Night Party," "Flight" and "Choir." Years later James Murphy of [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]] cited "Do the Du" as a reference point, Attack Magazine reports.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Attack Magazine
years.h: ACR opens for Talking Heads across the UK
years.p: [[Talking Heads|a94a7155-c79d-4409-9fcf-220cb0e4dc3a]] take the band on their December UK tour. Johnson says David Byrne watched their set every night.

eras.title: A loft in Tribeca, a drum kit in Prestwich
eras.text: Wilson rented the band a loft in New York and Hannett gave them his strangest instructions. They came back with a cover version recorded for £50, an indie number one, and a taste for Latin percussion that pulled them away from the Joy Division shadow and toward the dancefloor.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: A cassette in a plastic pouch: The Graveyard and the Ballroom
years.p: One side is Hannett's demos from Graveyard Studios in Prestwich; the other is live at the Electric Ballroom in Camden, October 1979.

years.src: Electronic Sound · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: "Shack Up" costs £50 in a basement in Prestwich
years.p: Topping brings in a 1975 Banbarra 45 bought for 50p. The band cuts it in a day, Kerr playing sheep jaw bones in the break, and in early 1981 it reaches No. 46 on Billboard's dance chart.
years.xp:
Topping found the single at Yanks, a Manchester shop selling deleted American records. The Graveyard Studio was a four-track in Stewart Pickering's basement on Church Road; Moscrop and Topping dug out the trumpets they'd played in school brass band.

"We were trying to copy it, but because we were non-musician punks, apart from Donald, it came out the other end sounding like it did," Moscrop told Electronic Sound.

years.src: Attack Magazine · Ban Ban Ton Ton · Write Wyatt · Wikipedia: To Each...
years.h: Hannett records To Each... in East Orange, New Jersey
years.p: Wilson puts the band up in a Tribeca loft for more than a month while [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]] works at E.A.R.S. studio. Johnson remembers Hannett's direction, word for word.
years.xp:
Johnson told Attack Magazine that Hannett was "off his head a lot of the time" and given to weird commands like the one above. With studio time left over, the support band ESG recorded their UFO EP, Ban Ban Ton Ton's interview recounts.

Hannett also cut backing tracks meant for [[Grace Jones|b1c124b3-cf60-41a6-8699-92728c8a3fe0]]. "She came down to the studio but didn't sing a note," Moscrop told Attack. Kerr says Chris Blackwell of Island stopped the project; the tapes, with Kerr's guide vocal, surfaced again some 40 years later.

years.cap: A Certain Ratio at the Rock Garden, London, February 1980
years.src: Ban Ban Ton Ton · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: "Flight" goes to No. 7 on the indie chart
years.p: A 12-inch, and in Moscrop's view the best thing the band did with Hannett. "He was really good at making a simple recording sound atmospheric," he told Ban Ban Ton Ton.

years.src: Wikipedia: To Each...
years.h: To Each... tops the UK indie chart
years.p: Twenty weeks on the chart. It closes with "Winter Hill," nearly 13 minutes long.

q: We thought he was making us sound too much like Joy Division
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Ban Ban Ton Ton
years.h: The band produces "Waterline" itself and drops Hannett
years.p: Another indie top ten, with more funk and jazz in it. Moscrop's reason for going it alone is below.
years.xp: Two decades later, [[Andrew Weatherall|4f4fd405-6ede-4da0-9b74-c422d8e09bed]] put "Waterline" on his Nine O'Clock Drop mix, and the band credit that with sending a new crowd back to the early records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sextet · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Sextet: Martha Tilson sings, Cuban drums, no Hannett
years.p: Recorded at Revolution Studios in Cheadle Hulme and self-produced. It tops the indie chart and makes the UK Top 75.
years.xp: [[Martha Tilson|27542a13-2476-4c3e-893e-f20e62d20bb3]]'s vocals gave the record an airier, more soulful feel. Stylus later called it a masterpiece, Pitchfork gave it 8.1; Trouser Press thought the band didn't "seem especially motivated."

years.cap: Promotional item for A Certain Ratio at the Haçienda, July 9, 1982
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: I'd Like to See You Again goes Latin disco
years.p: No. 2 on the indie chart. The NME heard ACR sounding like "the latest New York disco imports."

years.src: Attack Magazine · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Topping and Terrell leave; Kerr becomes the singer
years.p: Topping follows a girlfriend to New York and later forms T-Coy with Mike Pickering of Quando Quango. [[Andy Connell|b57d99e1-5149-418b-8194-09db8782edb7]] joins on keys and percussion.

years.cap: Handbill for A Certain Ratio with Madonna at Danceteria, New York, 1982
years.src: Attack Magazine · Ban Ban Ton Ton
years.h: Madonna plays her first show opening for ACR at Danceteria
years.p: Attack Magazine says she argued with the band about the stage setup. The [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] came to see ACR at Tier 3 on the same New York trips.

eras.title: Kerr at the mic, Connell out the door
eras.text: With two founders gone, the band leaned into soul and club records while its members fed half of Manchester's scene: Moscrop's side band Kalima, Connell's next one Swing Out Sister. The Factory years ended with Force.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Carol McKenzie sings "I Need Someone Tonight"
years.p: The comeback single goes top ten on the indie chart. Tony Quigley of Kalima joins on saxophone.

years.cap: Poster for A Certain Ratio at the Hoochie Coochie club, Edinburgh, December 6, 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Andy Connell leaves to start Swing Out Sister
years.p: "Wild Party" turns up in the film Letter to Brezhnev the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Force is the last ACR album on Factory
years.p: Made at Yello 2 Studios in Stockport with Corinne Drewery of Swing Out Sister guesting. Nine weeks on the indie chart, peaking at No. 2.

eras.title: Major-label money buys a studio
eras.text: A&M paid well enough for the band to build SoundStation, their own room in Manchester, then let them go after two albums. Rob Gretton's label carried them through the 1990s.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Write Wyatt · The Quietus
years.h: ACR signs to A&M and makes Good Together
years.p: Kerr, Moscrop, Johnson and Quigley are the band now. The money pays for SoundStation, their own studio in Manchester.
years.xp: Kerr didn't look back fondly. "We did sell ourselves out later on when we went to A&M and... we didn't sell out, we thought let's give it a go doing it this way... and it was a total mistake," he told the Quietus in 2010.

years.cap: NME on A Certain Ratio, July 14, 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: "Won't Stop Loving You" makes the UK Top 60, then A&M drops them
years.p: The single from acr:mcr peaks at No. 55 and pulls in a club crowd, but the deal ends after the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Attack Magazine
years.h: Rob Gretton's label puts out Up in Downsville
years.p: The New Order manager signs them to Rob's Records in 1991. Attack Magazine says that whenever the bailiffs came round, Gretton sent them away.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Ban Ban Ton Ton · Attack Magazine
years.h: Soundstation Volume 2 is the last release for years
years.p: It follows the 1996 album Change the Station. Gretton dies in 1999, aged 46, and the band steps back from records and touring.

eras.title: Better clothes, on film
eras.text: Weatherall's mix and Soul Jazz's reissues reintroduced the band to a generation of DJs, and Steve Coogan's Tony Wilson gave them a one-line review in the cinema. The band started playing again with no plan to stop.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Ban Ban Ton Ton
years.h: Coogan's Wilson: "all the energy of Joy Division but better clothes"
years.p: In 24 Hour Party People, Steve Coogan's Tony Wilson sizes up the band. Moscrop is the film's music supervisor, and Soul Jazz starts reissuing the early records.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: ACR plays America for the first time since 1985
years.p: They headline the Part Time Punks festival at the Echo in Los Angeles.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Mind Made Up includes the first song ACR ever wrote
years.p: "Teri" finally gets recorded. Denise Johnson, known for her work on Primal Scream's Screamadelica, sings.
years.xp: Kerr described the method to the Quietus: "songs being jammed in rehearsal one week and recorded the next." LTM reissued the album in 2010. Denise Johnson died in 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: A Factory night at Plan K in Brussels
years.p: ACR shares the bill with [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]], the Wake, the Names and Biting Tongues.

eras.title: Forty years on the floor
eras.text: Mute took over the catalogue, a box set laid out four decades, and the three men who'd been there since 1979 started writing again.

years.cap: A Certain Ratio at Wide Awake festival, London
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Mute signs the catalogue; "Dirty Boy" features Tony Wilson's voice
years.p: acr:set collects old tracks plus two new ones, including "Dirty Boy" with [[Barry Adamson|a50a1afa-23eb-4ba6-9faf-5dec260898ca]] of [[Magazine|043324ca-100d-48ce-8c7c-fd015afc103b]] and a recording of the late Wilson.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: acr:box puts 53 songs in one place
years.p: The 40th anniversary set comes with a tour.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio · Attack Magazine
years.h: ACR Loco: Kerr, Moscrop and Johnson, new songs
years.p: The first album of new material in 12 years, made with members of the live band.
years.xp: The band's working rule hadn't changed. "If a song became popular, we wouldn't write another one like it," Moscrop told Attack Magazine. Johnson: "People would come expecting to hear our new album and instead we've played new songs we just wrote that week."

years.cap: A Certain Ratio at New Century Hall, Manchester, April 22, 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
yt: Yo Yo Gi, New Century Hall, April 22, 2023
years.h: ACR plays New Century Hall, Manchester, the year of 1982
years.p: Their eleventh studio album came out the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Certain Ratio
years.h: Album twelve: It All Comes Down to This
years.p: Kerr, Moscrop and Johnson are still the core, 45 years after Johnson joined.
